Archimedes of Syracuse -LRB- -LSB- ˌɑːkɪˈmiːdiːz -RSB- Ἀρχιμήδης -RRB- was a Greek mathematician , physicist , engineer , inventor , and astronomer .	Greek	Greeks	mathematician	Greek mathematics	physicist	physics	engineer	engineering	inventor	inventor	astronomer	astronomy	Syracuse	Syracuse, Sicily
Although few details of his life are known , he is regarded as one of the leading scientists in classical antiquity .	classical antiquity	classical antiquity

Generally considered the greatest mathematician of antiquity and one of the greatest of all time , Archimedes anticipated modern calculus and analysis by applying concepts of infinitesimals and the method of exhaustion to derive and rigorously prove a range of geometrical theorems , including the area of a circle , the surface area and volume of a sphere , and the area under a parabola .	infinitesimals	infinitesimals	mathematician	Greek mathematics	calculus	calculus	analysis	mathematical analysis	method of exhaustion	method of exhaustion	geometrical	geometry	area	area	circle	circle	surface area	surface area	volume	volume	sphere	sphere	parabola	parabola

Other mathematical achievements include deriving an accurate approximation of pi , defining and investigating the spiral bearing his name , and creating a system using exponentiation for expressing very large numbers .	pi	pi	spiral	Archimedes spiral	exponentiation	exponentiation

He was also one of the first to apply mathematics to physical phenomena , founding hydrostatics and statics , including an explanation of the principle of the lever .	hydrostatics	Fluid statics	lever	lever	statics	statics

He is credited with designing innovative machines , such as his screw pump , compound pulleys , and defensive war machines to protect his native Syracuse from invasion .	screw pump	Archimedes' screw	compound pulleys	block and tackle	Syracuse	Syracuse, Sicily

Archimedes died during the Siege of Syracuse when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed .	Syracuse	Syracuse, Sicily	Siege of Syracuse	Siege of Syracuse (214–212 BC)	Roman	Roman Republic

Cicero describes visiting the tomb of Archimedes , which was surmounted by a sphere and a cylinder , which Archimedes had requested to be placed on his tomb , representing his mathematical discoveries .	sphere	sphere	Cicero	Cicero	cylinder	cylinder (geometry)
Unlike his inventions , the mathematical writings of Archimedes were little known in antiquity .

Mathematicians from Alexandria read and quoted him , but the first comprehensive compilation was not made until by Isidore of Miletus in Byzantine Constantinople , while commentaries on the works of Archimedes written by Eutocius in the sixth century AD opened them to wider readership for the first time .	Alexandria	Alexandria	Isidore of Miletus	Isidore of Miletus	Byzantine	Byzantine	Eutocius	Eutocius of Ascalon

The relatively few copies of Archimedes ' written work that survived through the Middle Ages were an influential source of ideas for scientists during the Renaissance , while the discovery in 1906 of previously unknown works by Archimedes in the Archimedes Palimpsest has provided new insights into how he obtained mathematical results .	Middle Ages	Middle Ages	Renaissance	Renaissance	Archimedes Palimpsest	Archimedes Palimpsest
